newsitem.title: GERMANY: Vietnam per-capita coffee use 835 grams - DKV.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam per-capita coffee use 835 grams - DKV.

text.p: Annual per-capita coffee consumption in Vietnam is currently 835 grams, the German coffee industry association DKV wrote in a newsletter.

In the article researched from a number of Asian sources, DKV said the country, Asia's second largest robusta producer, was consuming 61,000 tonnes of coffee a year on the basis of 73 million inhabitants.
DKV has said Japan tops Asian per-capita coffee consumption with 3.11 kg. Germany's comparable figure is 6.90 kg.
DKV also noted targets by national Vietnamese coffee strategists to raise total coffee production to 300,000 tonnes by the year 2000 from 240,000 tonnes currently.
DKV had received information that out of the current crop, some 179,000 tonnes should be exported, of which 176,550 tonnes should be robustas and 2,450 tonnes arabicas.
The export target for 2000 was 194,000 tonnes of robusta and 45,000 tonnes of arabica.
DKV also noted plans by the Vietnam Coffee and Cocoa Association (Vicofa) to raise arabica output to 100,000 tonnes by the year 2005.
